ROOT CAUSE FOUND (not the miter fix). bp_2967 walk-through = the adjacent STAIRS bp_2971 (130.5,286.5) ramp-trims bp_2967's wall collider to NOTHING. bp_2967 is depth-offset onto its floor → a thin x[129,129.25] strip that lies ENTIRELY inside the stairs footprint x[129,132], so trimBandRect (RAMPFOOT-0605) collapses the band below rampTrimMinBandMeters and returns null → fully passable. My miter commit (ed5ad0cd9) touches squareU/miter placement only — bands/depthSpan/ramp-trim are all unchanged by it, so this is independent (stairs-work territory, req_1700/1701). Fix is a stairs-vs-wall semantics call (a wall should never be fully nulled; side-walls along a ramp edge shouldn't be trimmed like risers across it) — awaiting user direction.

resolution: Fixed the bp_2967 walk-through. Root cause was NOT the corner-miter fix: the adjacent staircase bp_2971 ramp-trimmed bp_2967's wall collider to nothing. bp_2967 is depth-offset onto its floor, making a thin x[129,129.25] strip that sits entirely inside the stairs' x[129,132] plan footprint, so trimBandRect (RAMPFOOT-0605) collapsed the band below rampTrimMinBandMeters and returned null → a fully passable wall. Per the user's ruling ('wall always blocks'), trimBandRect now returns the wall band as-is instead of null when a trim would collapse it — partial ramp-foot trimming (flush to the ramp edge, keeping non-ramp mass) is unchanged; only the full-delete case is overridden. Verified bp_2967 now emits a blocking collider x[129,129.25] z[285,288] against the live world (was 0 rects); placed suite 57/57 green incl. the ramp-edge-trim and crest-wall-blocker tests; full game compile+bake+render GREEN.
